But Windows? I don't believe Windows actually uses Vulkan to render itself. So, why would a crash in Godot running over Vulkan cause an issue in Windows?

# My experience with fixing a similar issue on Linux:
## TL;DR:
For DRI_PRIME to work on Vulkan applications [vulkan-mesa-layers](https://archlinux.org/packages/?name=vulkan-mesa-layers) needs to be installed, as well as [lib32-vulkan-mesa-layers](https://archlinux.org/packages/?name=lib32-vulkan-mesa-layers) for 32 bit applications.

## Longer explanation:
Just wanted to share my experience with this issue.
Brief Specs (that I think are relevant): AMD CPU, NVIDIA 4070, additional AMD graphics card, Arch Linux based distro.

### What happens without vulkan-mesa-layers:
❯ godot
Godot Engine v4.4.stable.arch_linux - https://godotengine.org
OpenGL API 3.3.0 NVIDIA 570.124.04 - Compatibility - Using Device: NVIDIA - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070

Editing project: ***********
Godot Engine v4.4.stable.arch_linux - https://godotengine.org
Vulkan 1.4.305 - Forward+ - Using Device #0: AMD - AMD Radeon RX 5600 XT (RADV NAVI10)

ERROR: Condition "err != VK_SUCCESS" is true. Returning: ERR_CANT_CREATE
   at: swap_chain_resize (drivers/vulkan/rendering_device_driver_vulkan.cpp:3145)

ERROR: Condition "err != VK_SUCCESS" is true. Returning: ERR_CANT_CREATE
... (hangs and keeps repeating this error)

### What happens with vulkan-mesa-layers:
❯ godot
Godot Engine v4.4.stable.arch_linux - https://godotengine.org
OpenGL API 3.3.0 NVIDIA 570.124.04 - Compatibility - Using Device: NVIDIA - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070

Editing project: ***********
Godot Engine v4.4.stable.arch_linux - https://godotengine.org
Vulkan 1.4.303 - Forward+ - Using Device #0: NVIDIA - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070
...
and then it appears to be running fine.


I decided to try to be cheeky to run Godot with gamescope, just to see if there was any difference.
Initially gamescope reported using the wrong GPU for rendering. So I looked up how to switch gamescope to use the NVIDIA card.
Along this I found that I probably needed to install two packages listed on the Arch Wiki[https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/PRIME#For_open_source_drivers_-_PRIME]: 

For DRI_PRIME to work on Vulkan applications [vulkan-mesa-layers](https://archlinux.org/packages/?name=vulkan-mesa-layers) needs to be installed, as well as [lib32-vulkan-mesa-layers](https://archlinux.org/packages/?name=lib32-vulkan-mesa-layers) for 32 bit applications.

I installed these packages and didn't have this issue anymore. 
Perhaps someone more knowledgeable can let me know if they are required, 
or if there's something going on by adding these packages in my case of having multiple GPU's that allowed Godot to find a device to use (based on the desciption I found on what these packages do, it looks like they may help vulkan choose a device to use).

Maybe the wrong device is being chosen for some reason (in my case it looks like godot opens with the right device, then when opening a project to edit changes to the wrong device), or the device isn't found.
## Windows
Maybe there is a way to choose/guide which device to use through the vulkan tools available on Windows.

Hope this helps someone.

Using "get_tree().quit()" causing what looks like an intense graphics driver crash sporadically. I was a little outdated in drivers previously being on 581.15. I had the issue happen and tried looking into it and saw several posts in various places without much explanation. Just updated to up to date driver 591.74 and did a system restart just to clear up any possible lingering data in my system. 

First crash happened within the first few times, if not the first time, using get_tree().quit() to exit the in editor game test. Doing so froze both of my screens and my mouse right after. After about 15 seconds, both of my screens went black with the backlight in my panels still on. After about another 15 seconds the backlights turned off and my system beeped for disconnecting and reconnecting both monitors, shortly after both monitors came back on with. One monitor showed up a few seconds sooner with everything slowing popping back how it was prior to the crash, with the monitor Godot was on being solid black for a few seconds before it restored to my desktop with Godot being closed completely on it's own. 

After the first crash I did some research into the issue and found many posts about it being pretty unclear. I tried recreating the issue, hitting play in the editor for the same in editor playtest, and on the 19th get_tree().quit() the exact same crash happened. Wanting to get all the possible issues I can help with out of the way, I updated drivers. After a restart, I launched Godot and started testing again. After a bit I was feeling confident but on the 48th attempt the crash happened again in the same way. 

I guess this is just me trying to help out and give what info I can to lead to a fix. I like Godot and want to stick with it and avoid going back to Unity if at all possible. I just need to be able to properly and regularly playtest in the editor for it to be comfortable doing so. I plan on getting a Macbook for dev work within the next few months hopefully so if it's a windows only issue that's somewhat good for me, but I'd like it to be a smooth experience for everyone if possible.


Edit: 

I was being a little dramatic at the end there. I can confirm going into project settings, down to Rendering, in Rendering Device, switching Driver.windows from vulkan to d3d12 seems to have fixed the issue so far. I just finished 100 tests of get_tree().quit() on the same project and no repeated crashes so far. It's sad that Nvidia is likely not working properly with vulkan, but at least it's a simple fix when the issue is found for someone. it's just a bummer that there's an issue that some need to find a fix for like this at all.

TLDR: FIX: Going into project settings, down to Rendering, in Rendering Device, switching Driver.windows from vulkan to d3d12 seems to be the only fix.

Godot 4.6 should fix it by having d3d12 the default for all new projects in case you didn't read the post above(For those finding this through google like me).

Edit 2: I do get "pipeline_cache_create: PSO caching is not implemented yet in the Direct3D 12 driver." as a warning in the debugger after quitting the playtest. Just throwing that out as info for whoever can use it.

As far as I know, the only fix in 4.5.1 is to click the editor's stop button instead of the close button on the window. I've never had a crash doing it this way. You could also try switching rendering drivers from Vulkan to Direct3D 12 in your project settings (default for new projects in 4.6+), which would fix it if it's a Vulkan issue, but I haven't tried it personally, as I recently switched to Linux and don't have this issue there.

To change the driver, open project settings, show advanced settings, and change `rendering/rendering_device/driver.windows` to `d3d12`. Only change the `Driver.windows` setting and not the entire `Driver` setting. This change is recommended by Godot in the docs, but always check for weird specific cases where this causes bugs.
